{{Quote|Do you know why Valorum loves to attend the opera? Because it's the only place on Coruscant where an entire audience will applaud him.|Orn Free Taa|<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />}}
'''Finis Valorum''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Politics/Legends|politician]] who served as the penultimate [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. [[Reproduction/Legends|Born]] by [[87 BBY/Legends|87 BBY]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Valorum hailed from a highly regarded political [[House Valorum/Legends|family]], and after working through several challenging occupations he was elected as [[Senator/Legends|senator]] of the [[Lytton sector/Legends|Lytton sector]] through his family's connections. Valorum advocated against the development of a centralized Republic [[Army/Legends|army]], and came into prominence during the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]]. The conflict was a result of attacks on [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] [[Transport/Legends|transports]] by the [[Stark Commercial Combine]]. It was Valorum who advocated holding a summit with the Combine on the planet [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]], he also attended the summit along with several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].

The summit turned into an ambush when [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]], founder of the combine, revealed that he knew a fleet covertly assembled by Senator [[Ranulph Tarkin/Legends|Ranulph Tarkin]], Valorum's political enemy, was flying to Troiken to destroy the Combine. Stark sabotaged Tarkin's [[Starship/Legends|ships]] with a [[Tionese program|nanovirus]] that scrambled their [[Navigation computer/Legends|navcomputers]], and a firefight broke out in the meeting room. Valorum and the Jedi were able to escape and rendezvous with Tarkin's forces that made it planetside. After surviving attacks from Stark forces, Valorum and Gunray were escorted back to Coruscant by the Jedi [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]], where Valorum explained the situation to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] and prevented them from giving in to Stark's demands.

With his profile raised during the war, Valorum made a successful bid for [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] in [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]]. He won another term [[36 BBY/Legends|four]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, but was considered an ineffectual leader for his insistence on orthodox diplomatic approaches to issues. On the advice of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], a senator from the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and a close confidant of Valorum's, the Chancellor proposed [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]], instituting taxation [[Free Trade Zone/Legends|Free Trade Zones]]. The resolution severely impacted the Trade Federation's profits, causing the company to [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade]] Naboo. Valorum sent two Jedi; [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], on a secret mission to diplomatically solve the crisis.

Their attempt failed, but the Jedi managed to rescue [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of Naboo and brought her to Coruscant to present a plea for action to the Senate. Knowing that Valorum would be unable to effect any real progress, Palpatine convinced Amidala to call for a [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|Vote of No Confidence]] against Valorum, removing him from office. Palpatine was elected Chancellor, as he had orchestrated the entire crisis in a secret plan to restore [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|dominion]] over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. In retirement he wrote a biography; ''[[Holding Back the Tide]]'', and was visited by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] for information about the fate of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Remember Finis Valorum well, I do. Last of a great line, he was.|Yoda|<ref name="Shatterpoint">[[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Tarsus_Valorum-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Finis Valorum was part of a long lineage of politicians, including Tarsus Valorum (pictured).]]
Finis Valorum was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="NEGC" /> by around [[87 BBY/Legends|87 BBY]].<ref name="Age" /> He was the last in the line of [[House Valorum/Legends|House Valorum]],<ref name="Shatterpoint" /> a renowned [[Politics|political]] dynasty that included [[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]],<ref name="NEGC" /> who had served as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="Tarsus">{{CSWECite|Valorum, Tarsus|III|293}}</ref> Finis Valorum's own [[Finis Valorum's father|father]] was a politician,<ref name="FF56">{{FactFile|56|VAL 1-4|Finis Valorum}}</ref> who at some point failed to take action against the [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]], an act which would have consequences for Valorum's own career.<ref name="CoD">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> Valorum was expected to follow in his father's career,<ref name="FF56" /> and as a young man he received dozens of job offers from wealthy friends of his family. He instead chose challenging assignments that would test his character.<ref name="NEGC" />

One such assignment involved service as a [[Judge/Legends|judge]] in frontier conditions on the recently-discovered [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Republic protectorate|protectorate]] of [[Veccacopia]]<ref name="NEGC" /> in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Veccacopia system/Legends|Veccacopia system]]</ref> Unlike his predecessors in the post, Valorum worked hard to affect change; upon learning that the native [[Cacop]]s were hiring stand-ins to serve their sentences, as his bailiffs were unable to distinguish between individuals of the [[Species/Legends|species]], he instituted mandatory [[Eye/Legends|retinal]] scanning. His actions broke a corruption ring within Veccacopia's judicial office.<ref name="NEGC" />

After leaving Veccacopia, Valorum served with Republic police forces as a troop [[Transport/Legends|transport]] driver in the outlying regions. He later attained a post in the military advisory office of Supreme Chancellor [[Kalpana (Supreme Chancellor)/Legends|Kalpana]]. Valorum held elected office for the first time when he was in his late thirties, moving his residence from his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] to<ref name="NEGC" /> the planet<ref name="Spira">{{JournalCite|1|The Spira Regatta}}</ref> [[Spira/Legends|Spira]]. He was elected [[Senator/Legends|senator]] of the [[Lytton sector/Legends|Lytton sector]] based on his family's reputation and political contacts,<ref name="NEGC" /> to the surprise of no one. His background generated some resentment that followed him in his career,<ref name="FF56" /> though he rose through the unseen pecking order of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] quickly, making short-term allies and lasting enemies.<ref name="NEGC" /> Valorum quickly gained a reputation for being able to see and describe the bigger picture in issues, focusing on addressing the underlying causes rather than their symptoms.<ref name="FF56" />

Around [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]],<ref name="Fact File date">{{FactFile|56|VAL 1-4|Finis Valorum}} states that [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Valorum argued against a [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic army]] approximately thirty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], which began in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', placing his arguments around [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]].</ref> Valorum placed upon himself the responsibility to argue against the creation of a [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], speaking against its proponents;<ref name="FF56" /> which he dubbed the [[Militarists/Legends|Militarists]], including Senator [[Ranulph Tarkin/Legends|Ranulph Tarkin]] of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]]. Valorum was suspicious of Tarkin's motives, and Tarkin embraced the pejorative name in an effort to outflank Valorum.<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

===The Stark Hyperspace War===
====Advocate for peace====
{{Quote|A strong central military power would lead to abuses of power! Its existence would be a violation of Republic principles! It is our commitment to justice and freedom that rule us! The solution to this crisis lies in diplomacy.|Finis Valorum speaking to the Senate in the lead up to the Star Hyperspace War|<ref name="Stark1" />}}
In [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] shortage on the planet [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]] led to attacks by the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Stark Commercial Combine]] on many [[Transport/Legends|transports]] carrying the substance. Senators [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and Tarkin argued for an increase in military power in the Senate. Valorum argued against militarization, believing it to be a violation of Republic principles and calling for a diplomatic solution that addressed the shortage's underlying causes. To do so, Valorum arranged a summit on the Outer Rim planet [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]] between the Stark Combine, the Trade Federation, and Republic representatives, with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tyvokka/Legends|Tyvokka]] serving as chief negotiator. Shortly before the summit, Valorum met with a delegation from the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], including Tyvokka, [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]], and Tyvokka's former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], who was not a Council member at the [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="Stark1" />

At the meeting, Tyvokka asserted his suspicions that the bacta shortage was legitimate, due to the profits its scarcity had brought to the Trade Federation and the [[Vratix/Legends|Thyferrans]]. Valorum asked if the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] had any proof, which was unavailable, but Tyvokka suggested that the Jedi [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] and his Padawan [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] [[Mission to Thyferra|investigate]]. Tyvokka asked to take Koon, [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to Troiken, and Valorum requested Gallia's presence as an [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]]. The Republic delegates along with Gunray arrived first, but after [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]] and the other leadership of the Combine arrived the meeting took a sour turn. Stark revealed that he knew a [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Navy]] covertly assembled by Tarkin was flying to Troiken to trap him, which Valorum assured had been done without the knowledge of anyone present. Stark had prepared a [[Tionese program|computer virus]], which sabotaged the [[Navigation computer/Legends|navcomputers]] of the Navy's vessels. The virus led to the destruction of many ships in faulty [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jumps, while Tarkin's personal flagship, the [[Invincible (Stark Hyperspace War)|''Invincible'']],<ref name="Stark1" /> and only a third of his forces arrived at Troiken, immediately [[First Battle of Qotile|attacked]] by Stark's ships, beginning the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]].<ref name="Stark2">[[Star Wars (1998) 37|''Star Wars'' (1998) 37]]</ref>

[[File:The_Troiken_crew.png|thumb|left|300px|Valorum and the other Republic delegates in the aftermath of the ambush on Troiken]]
With his hand revealed, Stark ordered the Republic delegates to surrender, but Tyvokka threw the conference room's table in the air, leading to a firefight. The [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] Jedi ordered Gallia to protect Valorum, which she had already anticipated. Most of Stark's personnel in the conference room, aside from the Combine leadership, was [[Death/Legends|killed]] and Tyvokka was injured by friendly fire from Gunray's [[HKB-3 hunter-killer droid]]. The Republic delegates knew they had to leave to get to safety, with Valorum and Koon supporting Tyvokka as they left the conference room. After reaching their [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]], Valorum contacted Tarkin via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]], chastising him for the turn of events and providing coordinates on Troiken where his [[Trooper/Legends|troops]] could land. Valorum's plan was for the [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] to land near [[Mount Avos]] and retreat into its caves. Tarkin was outraged and insisted that [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] belonged to him, but as the ''Invincible'' took more damage and began to fall onto Troiken's surface, Valorum responded that the choice had been made for him.<ref name="Stark2" />

====Bold action====
{{Quote|It's said the reason the Republic did not surrender to Stark's demands was solely because of Senator Valorum.|Adi Gallia|<ref name="Stark4">[[Star Wars (1998) 39|''Star Wars'' (1998) 39]]</ref>}}
After Tarkin escaped his doomed ship, Valorum explained to the Jedi that he could not ensure Tarkin's compliance. Gunray insisted that the group head to his own [[Trade Federation shuttle|shuttle]], but Stark forces immediately destroyed it. Jinn knew it meant the Combine knew their location and instructed the ship's [[Unidentified Galactic Republic captain|captain]] to take them to the rendezvous point, in spite of the ship's damaged condition. Tyvokka's state deteriorated in the journey, in his dying moments he instructed Koon to prioritized Valorum's safety.<ref name="Stark2" /> After learning near Mount Avos the Republic delegates had to quickly leave the ship, knowing it was about to explode. Tarkin met with the group and blamed Valorum for their circumstances and planned to say as much to the Senate, which Valorum retorted that he would have difficulty explaining his unauthorized army to the Senate. Koon insisted that they continue the discussion from the safety of the mountain. Gunray and Tarkin suggested suing for peace with Stark, an action Valorum decried as nonsense as they still had troops available and the mountain could protect them from [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombardment]].<ref name="Stark3">[[Star Wars (1998) 38|''Star Wars'' (1998) 38]]</ref>

[[File:Valorum_senator.png|thumb|right|250px|Senator Valorum's profile was raised during the Stark Hyperspace War.]]
Tarkin's [[Army/Legends|army]] and the Jedi held off Stark's forces in the [[Second Battle of Qotile]], after which Koon insisted that the group prioritize returning Valorum to Coruscant to explain their situation. Tarkin's [[Aide/Legends|aide]] [[Jace Dallin]] launched a diversionary [[Third Battle of Qotile|attack]] while Valorum, Gunray, Gallia, Jinn, Kenobi, and the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] used a transport to reach a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]. They planned to steal Stark's personal ship, the [[Quicksilver (Iaco Stark)|''Quicksilver'']]. A sudden explosion caused by Tholme and Vos, who had arrived on Troiken, provided a necessary diversion that allowed Gallia to get Gunray, Valorum, and the pilot onboard the ''Quicksilver'' and departed.<ref name="Stark3" /> As the ship came out of hyperspace near Coruscant a booby trap on the controls activated, killing the pilot. Gallia ordered Gunray and Valorum into [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]], which were collected by [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Forces]]. Valorum convinced the ground personnel of his identity and demanded a hearing in the Senate. He persuaded the Senate to refrain from surrendering to Stark, convincing the senators that they only needed to replace the infected navicomputers. The Republic decided to prioritize trade vessels, but would not act to save the troops left on Troiken due to their unauthorized presence. Valorum afterwards met with Windu and Gallia and apologized that he could not do more.<ref name="Stark4" />

Windu was able to acquire the [[Trade Defense Force]] to save the soldiers on Troiken and end the war. Tarkin insisted on detonating an explosive to trap Stark forces inside the mountain in the [[Fifth Battle of Qotile|last battle]], in an attempt to preserve his own legacy and be remembered as hero. Valorum's actions during the war made him a rising star in the Senate and contributed to his running as Supreme Chancellor.<ref name="Stark4" />

===Supreme Chancellor===
====First Year====
[[File:Inhischambers.jpg|thumb|left|240px|Valorum is visited by Jedi in his office.]]
Valorum won [[Supreme Chancellor election, 40 BBY|election]] to his first term as Supreme Chancellor of the Republic in [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]], with the support of the [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]]. Their aid hinged on the condition that Valorum posthumously decorate Ranulph Tarkin for his role in the resolution of the Stark Hyperspace War.<ref name="NEC" /> As Chancellor, Valorum declared Ranulph Tarkin the "Hero of [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]]," resulting in an increase in support for Militarism.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Valorum's election was perceived as hollow and cynical by many; his enemies believed he would be easy to control, his allies supported him only because they felt that he was the best prospect in an unremarkable group of candidates, and the public knew nothing about him other than his famous surname. He was also perceived as lacking charisma.<ref name="NEGC" />

That year,<ref name="Witness date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places the events of ''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Only Witness]]'' in [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]].</ref> Chancellor Valorum called a special hearing of the entire Senate on the corruption of the [[Cobral family]] on the planet [[Frego]], including its links to Senator [[Crote (Human)|Crote]]. Testimony was given by family defector [[Lena Cobral]], and when she arrived at the Convocation Chamber, Valorum gave her a signal to speak. Following Lena's testimony the Senate quickly voted to remove Crote from office and the Cobral family was ordered to be placed under arrest.<ref name="Only Witness">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Only Witness]]''</ref> As Chancellor, Valorum was a fan of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi completed multiple missions on the Chancellor's behalf, which often paired them with Adi Gallia and her Padawan [[Siri Tachi/Legends|Siri Tachi]].<ref name="NEC" />

====The Vena negotiations====
{{Quote|Chancellor Valorum was most influential in the negotiations. Of course&hellip; He didn't really have a choice. One more false move and I'll make the guards shoot him.|Baroness Omnino, taking Valorum hostage in front of Jinn and Kenobi|<ref name="Ord Mantell 3">[[Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell 3|''Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell'' 3]]</ref>}}
[[File:Chancellorandconsort.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Valorum and Taria waiting for Baroness Omnino on Coruscant]]
One [[Standard day/Legends|night]]<ref name="Ord Mantell 1">[[Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell 1|''Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell'' 1]]</ref> in [[37 BBY/Legends|37 BBY]],<ref name="Ord Mantell date">[[Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell 1|''Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell'' 1]] is stated to take place five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Therefore, the events of the [[Star Wars: Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell|''Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell'']] series take place in [[37 BBY/Legends|37 BBY]].</ref> Valorum and his [[Senior Administrative Aide/Legends|Staff Aide]] [[Sei Taria/Legends|Sei Taria]] waited on a [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]] landing platform as the ship ''[[Benevolent III]]'' carried [[Baroness/Legends|Baroness]] [[Omnino]] of the planet [[Vena]] to Coruscant. Valorum hoped to persuade Omnino to allow Vena to join the Republic, as its supplies could support Coruscant for generations. The Chancellor asked Taria if the baroness had been followed, as she had been targeted for death by the [[Vena Isolationists]], but Taria assured him that precautions had been taken. Valorum hoped that the [[Senate Guard/Legends|Senate Guards]] would be appropriate protection, as Omnino rejected a Jedi escort.<ref name="Ord Mantell 1" />

Taria postulated that the baroness would not have come to Coruscant without benefitting herself. She stated that if Omnino wanted to open a trade route to Vena they would need the Republic's support to resolve the [[Venan civil war|civil war]] in the [[Vena system/Legends|Vena system]]. Valorum personally greeted Omnino when she arrived, for which she thanked him. The proceedings were interrupted when a [[Unidentified Senate Guard (mind control)|Senate guard]]<ref name="Ord Mantell 1" />&mdash;mind-controlled by a device worn by Omnino to gain sympathy in the Senate<ref name="Ord Mantell 3" />&mdash; suddenly tried to murder the baroness. Qui-Gon Jinn had been disguised as a Senate guard and saved Omnino with his [[Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], and the failed [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] leapt to his death from the landing platform rather than face capture. As Omnino's [[Omnino's bodyguard|bodyguard]] had been killed by the assassin, Valorum tried to offer her Jedi protection but was initially rebuffed. The following morning however, Omnino reneged and requested Jinn's protection, despite the animosity between them for the Jedi's failure to protect her [[Kindoro|husband]] years earlier. Omnino was expected to meet with Valorum and a group of senators, but it was postponed until Omnino's son [[Sando (Baron)|Sando]] arrived on Coruscant. In the meantime, Valorum arranged a tour of the [[Holographic Zoo of Extinct Animals]] for the baroness.<ref name="Ord Mantell 1" />

While Omnino met with Jinn and Kenobi and admired the exhibits, Valorum and Taria arrived to bear unfortunate news. The chancellor explained that a distress signal from Sando's ship had been detected in the [[Bright Jewel Cluster/Legends|Bright Jewel Cluster]], far away from Vena. Valorum explained that an emergency response team was en route, but Omnino requested that Jinn [[Mission to the Bright Jewel Cluster|investigate]] instead,<ref name="Ord Mantell 1" /> as part of a ploy to discredit the Jedi. The investigation uncovered Sando's involvement in gathering [[Mantellian Savrip/Legends|Savrips]] from the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], where Omnino had been in league with the [[land baron]] [[Taxer Sundown]]. In the meantime, Omnino participated in negotiations that resulted in Vena joining the Republic. Her fabricated assassination attempt resulted in a Senate sympathetic to her, and she used her mind control device to ensure that Valorum was instrumental in securing her favored outcome. Republic membership gave Omnino unlimited access to Ord Mantell, which she traveled to following the negotiations aboard the ''Benevolent III'' with Valorum and several mind-controlled Senate Guards.<ref name="Ord Mantell 3" />

[[File:Valorum_hostage.png|thumb|left|300px|A mind-controlled Valorum held hostage on Ord Mantell]]
Omnino had planned to rendezvous with Sundown, but arrived just after he had been dispatched by Jinn and Kenobi, who had allied with the Savrips. The Jedi met with the baroness and she revealed her plan, and used the Senate Guards to hold Valorum hostage in front of the Jedi. Jinn resolved the situation by offering to leave the Jedi Order and work as Omnino's guardian, and when she let her guard down he decapitated her to end her mind controlling influence. Valorum was shocked to see her corpse, as he had no memory from being controlled, and Jinn explained her duplicitous actions. He then watched as Jinn railed against several Human Mantellian colonists after one of them shot the Savrip [[Mawkran]], explaining that the Savrip species had been misunderstood as monsters. Valorum traveled back to Coruscant with the Jedi, expressing his gratitude while explaining that the Senate would insist on an investigation.<ref name="Ord Mantell 3" />

====Second Term====
Despite the aforementioned disadvantages, combined with his apparent lack of charisma, Valorum [[Supreme Chancellor election, 36 BBY/Legends|won]] a second four-year term in office<ref name="NEGC" /> in [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> albeit by a very slim margin. What little support Valorum still enjoyed vanished as he failed to overcome the apathy and dishonesty that afflicted the Republic,<ref name="NEGC" /> and opposing parties began to consider possible replacements for him, often considering Senator [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]],<ref name="NEC" /> who was one of Valorum's oldest political friends<ref name="NEGC" /> and had become a member of his inner circle.<ref name="TEA" />

Valorum had become embattled by [[34 BBY/Legends|34 BBY]], when the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] launched a [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the [[Malastare Narrows/Legends|Malastare Narrows]] during a dispute over fuel allocations from [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]], which appealed to the Chancellor to intervene after efforts to reach a diplomatic solution failed. Valorum feared that the Alliance could achieve victory, as the [[Dustig Sector Forces]] were weakened by corruption and neglect, so he demurred publicly while covertly convincing the neighboring [[Tyus sector/Legends|Tyus]] and [[Var Hagen sector/Legends|Var Hagen sectors]] to support Malastare. He also diverted [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to the [[Dug/Legends|Dugs]] to hire [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]] and dispatched the Jedi [[Kep-She/Legends|Kep-She]] and an officer named [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]] to the area, ostensibly as military observers. Although the subsequent [[Battle of Malastare Narrows/Legends|Battle of Malastare Narrows]] forced the Corporate Alliance to retreat, scandal ensued, embarrassing the already-troubled Valorum.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

After the [[Dorvalla Incident]] in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], on the initiative of Senator Palpatine, Valorum suggested for the taxation of Free-Trade routes to make peace with the Nebula Front who had been terrorizing the Trade Federation. The Front did not think this would make any difference and attempted to murder the Chancellor. The terrorists made two assassination attempts, both of which were foiled by the Jedi.<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />

Shortly afterwards, Palpatine secretly funneled several million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], believed to have been stolen by the Nebula Front, through the [[Bank of Aargau/Legends|Bank of Aargau]], and into the accounts of the Valorum family. Palpatine's aide, [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]], ensured that the exchange was uncovered by Valorum's political enemy, Senator [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]], who revealed it to the [[Internal Activities Committee/Legends|Internal Activities Committee]], thus critically weakening the Chancellor's already tenuous hold on power.<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />

Although Valorum denied the accusations and his supporters rallied to his side, his influence and reputation languished. Correctly thinking that he could be ousted from his charge in a near future, Valorum then decided to perform one last good deed while he could, and he gathered the Coruscant security forces to fight a subversive organization known as [[the Flail]]. The Flail, who believed the Senate was corrupt, had performed several attacks, disrupting public services with no care for the lives or property lost. The Flail's members dwindled thanks to Valorum's efforts, and the main leaders of the conspiracy died in a shooting with the police. Valorum publicly promised that the remnants of the Flail would be taken to justice before the following Senate conference, which prompted the new terrorist leader, [[Zegmon Pent]], to send Valorum death threats and vainly assault his Staff Aide Sei Taria.<ref name="SOC">{{WizCite|book=Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook|story=Shadows of Coruscant}}</ref>

During this time, Valorum had strengthened his ties with the Jedi, and he asked Jedi Master and Council member Mace Windu for advice. Windu and Valorum had deduced that the Flail would attack Valorum during his next public speech. Windu noticed that the Flail tended to flee when noticing a known member of the [[Senate Guard/Legends|Senate Guard]] or the Council; he thus suggested Valorum to create a strike force of relatively unknown but well-recommended agents. Valorum agreed and, again with Windu's help, compiled some candidates and called them for a meeting. While Valorum and Windu were to meet this new secret police in person soon afterwards, Valorum himself was delayed and arrived shamefully late.<ref name="SOC" />

[[File:Valorum-SWE.png|thumb|right|180px|Chancellor Valorum]]
Windu explained that the Flail would probably attack Valorum from the [[Weather Modulation Control Center]] and/or from the [[Air Traffic Control]]. The new team went to the Weather Center and fought with several anarchists who wanted to reprogram the weather and cause a threatening thunderstorm that could damage the buildings in the speech area. As soon as the combat was over, Valorum personally contacted them, to be know whether any of them had [[Death/Legends|died]] or not and to offer his help. The Flail, including Pent himself, then tried to attack Valorum from the Air Traffic Control by sending a remote-piloted vehicle to crash in the meeting area. While Valorum was giving his conference, his new agents ended with the threat of the Flail.<ref name="SOC" />

===The Naboo crisis===
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Trade Federation made use of their [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|battleships]] in a practically impenetrable blockade orbiting [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. It was a bold move for the usually cowardly Federation, triggering the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Naboo crisis]].<ref name="Episode I" />

For the next month, the Senate debated fiercely, but did not act to aid the people of Naboo. The Federation's representative, Lott Dod, successfully argued his case: they had not violated any Republic laws; they had attacked no ships, nor had they moved against Naboo itself. And if no outright crime had been committed, the Judicial Department could not be sent. The stalling further weakened the Valorum administration; their defiance of his measures was in itself damaging to the Chancellor's already dwindling support.

[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] of Naboo contacted Valorum and held him personally responsible for the suffering on her world. Every day he delayed, she stated, he took [[Bread/Legends|bread]] out of the mouths of the starving [[Youngling/Legends|children]] of Naboo. Pressed against the wall by his conscience, and desperate to shore up his crumbling support, he decided to act. He would call for a special session of the Senate to discuss the blockade, but to have a strong bargaining position, he needed the battleships sent home from Naboo. He would use the Jedi as ambassadors and send them to Naboo. Their presence would shake the Neimoidians' confidence and show them he meant business.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> But this came to nothing as the Federation occupied Naboo and detained Amidala. In a daring raid, she was rescued by the two Jedi Valorum had sent; Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi. Valorum met the Queen when she arrived on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to assure her that necessary steps were being taken to end the crisis.<ref name="Episode I" />

===Removal from office===
{{Quote|I will ''not'' defer. I have come before you to resolve this attack on our sovereignty now! I was not elected to watch my people suffer and die while you discuss this invasion in a committee. If this body is not capable of action, I suggest new leadership is needed. I move for a Vote of No Confidence in Chancellor Valorum's leadership."<br />"Now they will elect a new Chancellor.. .a strong Chancellor. One who will not let this tragedy continue.|[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:ZodKneelsBeforeAmidala-TPMHD.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Valorum reacts to the Vote of No Confidence.]]
The long-anticipated special session of the Senate&mdash;the last under the Valorum government&mdash;had only two items on its agenda: a hearing of the Naboo delegation's case, and a debate on the Trade Federation's continued opposition to [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]]. Few expected it to be anything other than routine.<ref name="Episode I novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]], the Federation's representative, stalled the proceedings with every procedural tool at his command.<ref name="Episode I" />

Dod and his allies threw up objection after objection; Amidala, unable to even finish her plea, grew more and more frustrated. Finally, Dod moved that a Senate committee be created to go to Naboo to determine if her "accusations" were valid, citing senatorial procedures that Amidala had no hope of understanding.<ref name="Episode I" /> Then, [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]]&mdash;as expected&mdash;pulled Valorum aside, subtly forcing Valorum to concede that Dod was within his rights according to [[Section 523A]].<ref name="Episode I novel" /> "''Enter the bureaucrats''," Palpatine whispered into the queen's ear, "''the true rulers of the Republic, and on the payroll of the Trade Federation, I might add. This is where Chancellor Valorum's strength will disappear.''" When Valorum turned back from Amedda and asked the queen if she would defer her motion to allow the committee to do its work, it was the last straw. She had seen with her own eyes that Palpatine had been right&ndash;Valorum ''was'' ineffective&ndash;and she had nowhere left to go. Amidala delivered the words that sealed Finis Valorum's fate: a [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|Vote of No Confidence]].<ref name="Episode I" />

Valorum was surprised by the motion, never anticipating the betrayal - events had moved past him. Senator [[Edcel Bar Gane/Legends|Edcel Bar Gane]] of [[Roona/Legends|Roona]] seconded Amidala's motion, and the vote was on the floor. The Senate had waited for this for months, perhaps years, and so unpopular was Valorum that there was little resistance to removing him from office.<ref name="Episode I novel" /> The senators erupted into a frenzied uproar, calling out, "''Vote now! Vote now! Vote now!''"<ref name="Episode I" /> All the Chancellor could do was to postpone the vote until the following day. When the Senate convened the following day to vote on the no confidence motion, the outcome was decisive. Valorum had few friends left, and the Senate so badly wanted him gone that they did not hesitate. Finis Valorum was swiftly voted out and with his political career in ruins, he was left to start his life over from scratch.<ref name="Episode I" />

===Retirement===
{{Quote|It's been a long time, my friend.|Valorum, to Yoda, during the Clone Wars|<ref name="The Lost One">{{TCW|The Lost One}}</ref>}}
[[File:Valorum_Yoda_The_Lost_One.png|thumb|right|300px|Valorum meets with Yoda during the Clone Wars.]]
After his resignation, Valorum spent the next two years in seclusion, waiting for the public's distaste for him to wear off. He contributed where he could and received no thanks for his trouble. After he returned to public life, he spent his retirement working with the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]].<ref name="Dead Ends" /> He also wrote an autobiography, ''[[Holding Back the Tide]]'', which was released in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] to poor sales and little interest.<ref name="HNN Books">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|life/13314_3.html|Valorum & Gunray Bracket Ends of Book Sales}}</ref> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], he participated in a Refugee Relief Movement project to construct housing for refugees from [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] worlds on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], using a [[power-shovel]] to dig postholes for the prefabricated structures.<ref name="HNN Alderaan">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|news/13328_2.html|Alderaan Opens to Refugee Relief Movement}}</ref> Later that year, he attended a Refugee Relief Movement fundraiser at the [[Xenvaer Civic Auditorium]] on [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]].<ref name="HNN Twang">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|life/13425_1.html|SPECIAL FEATURE: Sightings by Twang}}</ref>

During the Clone Wars, Valorum was visited at his estate by Master Yoda, who was on a quest to discover the fate of Jedi Master [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]]. Valorum provided Yoda information about a meeting he set up between Sifo-Dyas, his personal aide [[Silman/Legends|Silman]], an unknown Jedi, and the [[Pyke Syndicate/Legends|Pyke Syndicate]] prior to Sifo-Dyas's disappearance.<ref name="The Lost One" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|It's the spirit of helping one another that has made this Republic great, and will see it through its darker hours.|Finis Valorum|<ref name="HNN Alderaan" />}}
[[File:FinisValorum.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The last vestige of a once great lineage of Supreme Chancellors]]
Valorum came from an antediluvian line of distinguished aristocrats, two of whom having served as Chancellor in the past (one of them, [[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]], being the first elected Chancellor for four hundred years prior to his administration that was not a Jedi). This background, ironically, worked against him, as many came to believe he had been elected solely by means of hereditary inheritance rather than by means of the electorate.

Valorum was the one who instituted the fashion among the [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] elite of going to operas; it was joked among his political enemies that he enjoyed them because they were the only places where he could get any applause. He had a taste for exotic and expensive things, and his office during his Chancellorship was furnished with many antique and rare items.

Amidst all of his faults, he did have some redeeming graces. During the Naboo invasion, he was, as quoted by Queen Amidala, their strongest supporter.<ref name="Episode I" /> He also called an emergency conference of the Senate to either relegate the Trade Federation's movements, or punish them outright. Unfortunately, his more political characteristics were during the conference when in a hushed conversation with his [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chairman]] Mas Amedda and Staff Aide Sei Taria.<ref name="Cloak of Deception" /> During this time, Senator Palpatine revealed to Queen Amidala that the leadership of the Galactic Republic was also, aside from their substantial government stipends, on an additional payroll of none other than the Trade Federation. This revelation alone was proof enough of the Chancellor's corruption, which ultimately led to Amidala's plea for a Vote of No Confidence in place of Valorum.<ref name="Episode I" /> Taken off guard by this, the Supreme Chancellor could do little more than sit down in his seat and await the coming chaos.<ref name="Episode I novel" />

Valorum was also known for his connections with various women. He had close ties with Jedi Master Adi Gallia<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />; was rumored to be having an affair with his Staff Aide, Sei Taria, during his chancellorship;<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> and after his retirement from politics, was sighted in the companionship of a "doe-eyed blonde number."<ref name="HNN Twang" />

==Equipment==
During the Naboo crisis, Valorum wielded a [[Ceremonial staff (Finis Valorum)|ceremonial staff]] adorned with the [[Galactic Great Seal]],<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|pack=Chancellor Valorum|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeIvalorum.asp}}</ref> a symbol of the Republic.<ref name="Encyclopedia">{{CSWECite|I|310|Galactic Great Seal}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I said, 'What's he like, the president of the universe?' And George Lucas said, 'He's a good man but he's beleaguered&mdash;a bit like [Bill] Clinton.' That was before Clinton was as beleaguered as he is now, of course.|[[Terence Stamp]], in a [[1998]] interview with ''[[Star Wars Insider]]''|<ref name="Stamp of Approval">{{InsiderCite|41|Terence Stamp: Stamp of Approval}}</ref>}}
Valorum was portrayed by actor [[Terence Stamp]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="Episode I" /> and was voiced by [[Ian Ruskin]] in the TV series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''.<ref name="The Lost One" /> Stamp, who filmed all of Valorum's scenes against a blue screen, took the role of Valorum because he felt that the character was not a one-dimensional cameo, and he wanted to work with [[George Lucas]], the creator of ''[[Star Wars]]'' and the writer and director of ''The Phantom Menace''. Stamp did not have much time to prepare for the role and was unable to read the full script, so he felt he did not have much to base his character on. To understand what Valorum was like, Lucas told Stamp that Valorum was similar to then-[[Wikipedia:President of the United States|United States President]] [[Wikipedia:Bill Clinton|Bill Clinton]], describing Valorum as "a good man but he's beleaguered," though Stamp noted that this was prior to Clinton's impeachment trial.<ref name="Stamp of Approval" /><ref name="economicexpert">{{WebCite|url=http://www.economicexpert.com/a/Supreme:Chancellor:Valorum.html|text=economicexpert|nobackup=1}}</ref>

In the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Valorum (The Star Wars)|Valorum]] (a [[Knights of Sith|Knight of Sith]]) was intended to be a dark, masked prince&mdash;a role similar to the [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] known today, even to the extent of changing sides at the end of the film and siding with the heroes.<ref name="Rough Draft">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-star-wars-rough-draft|text=''The Star Wars: Rough Draft''|work=[https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller Starkiller — The Jedi Bendu Script Site]|archivedate=20240601042406}}</ref>

===Original fate===
{{Quote|The Senate barters away fundamental rights upon which the Republic was built! You trust that the tyrant you are creating will give them back to you when the crisis is over? Palpatine will give back nothing! No one who seeks power the way that he does ever surrenders it willingly!&hellip; Palpatine will make sure that any individual or group that opposes him or is in his way is removed! Look what happened to King Veruna! Look what happened to me! I know it was Palpatine who had me framed. I was forced to resign as Chancellor so he could ascend to it! Just as I am certain he arranged for those pirates to attack your transport!&hellip; I have no more proof of that than I do that he masterminded my fall. If I did have it, Palpatine would be in chains this moment.|Finis Valorum, to Bail Organa|<ref name="Dead Ends" />}}
In [[Republic 61|''Republic'' 61]], around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], Finis Valorum reappeared in politics. Valorum had observed Palpatine's activities, both public and private, from a distance, especially how the Chancellor's opponents, like [[Seti Ashgad/Legends|Seti Ashgad]], had a habit of disappearing. Possibly the [[Enhanced Security and Enforcement Act|Enforcement Act]] had been the last straw in a string of offenses which forced Valorum into action. But Palpatine had ears everywhere, even in custodial droids working in [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa's]] residence at [[Cantham House/Legends|Cantham House]], so when Valorum came to visit Organa there, it was not long before comments like this reached the Chancellor's desk.<ref name="Dead Ends" />

What Palpatine thought of Valorum's words is unknown, but they clearly buttressed Organa's courage, so the next morning he appeared at the Chancellor's Suite to insist that under no circumstances would he support the Enforcement Act, and that in fact he would ''oppose'' Palpatine on it. The Chancellor said nothing about it, but told Organa that it was in his best interest not to see Valorum again.<ref name="Dead Ends" />

[[File:Iskin2.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The ''[[Star of Iskin]]'' explodes, killing Finis Valorum.]]
Valorum was murdered in a terrorist attack shortly after the [[Battle of Jabiim]], when his freighter, ''[[Star of Iskin]]'', exploded on takeoff. The attack was secretly orchestrated by Darth Sidious, but publicly attributed to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], in an attempt to get rid of Valorum because he had been talking to Senator Organa about Palpatine's political maneuverings.<ref name="Dead Ends" /> In truth, apparently upon the machinations of Darth Sidious, Finis Valorum was murdered by [[Anzat (species)|Anzati]] assassin [[Sajé Tasha]], upon the behest of the corrupt Senator [[Viento]] upon orders by [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]]. This information would later be used by [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] in his hunt for the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], though it would lead him to believe that Viento, and later Bulq, was the elusive "Second Sith" whom Dooku had mentioned to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] three years before.<ref name="Trackdown">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Trackdown]]''</ref>

The [[Finis Valorum Memorial]] was constructed on Coruscant to honor the last being who served as Chancellor before Palpatine's rise to power. Only 200 people attended the opening ceremony. Future generations, however, would look more kindly on him.

This article assumes that the parts of the comic in 22 BBY are still canon, though the above information surrounding Valorum's death has likely since been overwritten by the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[The Lost One]]," which shows him alive in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], probably about a year after his death is presumably depicted in ''Dead Ends''.
